rationale: All five ticket acceptance criteria (AC1-AC5) pass — the primary fix correctly scopes _collect_files_from_conversation to the latest turn with files, the secondary fix removes the silent all-files fallback, and the regression test reproduces + verifies AC2. However three actionable issues surfaced across the lenses: (a) the mixin fix's empty-return interacts badly with the attachment-tool call sites — a null/empty file param coerces to a truthy list and bypasses the 'no names requested' guard, so filter returns {} and both GenericJiraIssueTool and GenericConfluenceTool silently fall through their attachment branch to the plain API path; (b) the primary fix's max(history_index) selector operates on all roles despite the ticket wording 'most recent USER turn' — UpsertHistoryRequest accepts arbitrary-role GeneratedMessage via REST, letting an assistant-role message with file_names shadow the real user turn; (c) if the user edits their latest turn to REMOVE all files, that turn drops out of messages_with_files, and the selector falls back to a prior turn's files — the very leak the fix was meant to prevent, in a narrow but plausible edge case. 2 findings dismissed as cosmetic/design (mock semantics latent-only, comment mentions only one of two callers) — see follow_ups. No security or standards violations. Confidence low because CR-003 needs a product decision (accept the edge case, or scope more strictly).

business_review.notes: utils.py: max(history_index)-with-files selection discards earlier turns.
test_second_attach_turn_does_not_include_first_turn_file reproduces the ticket scenario and asserts only test2.png returned.
Two-layer scoping (utils + mixin) applied; GenericJiraIssueTool.execute chains both before _handle_file_attachments.
Cross-turn history accumulation removed at root; dict-keyed dedup preserved for current+latest-history overlap.
4 tests in test_file_collection_scoping.py + 5 tests in test_file_tool_mixin.py; the reproducer test exercises the real max-history_index selection (patches only bypass DB/FileService).

standards_review.notes: All 4 commits use type(EPMCDME-12227): subject and reference the ticket.
Pre-commit ruff format+lint passed on every commit.

findings.problem: A file param carrying an empty string or null (e.g. {"file": ""} / {"file": null} / {"files": [null]}) is coerced to a single-element truthy list, bypassing the `if not requested_file_names: return all_files` guard. The loop matches nothing, filter returns {}. Callers gate their attachment path on `if requested_files:` (GenericJiraIssueTool jira/tools.py:139, GenericConfluenceTool confluence/tools.py:~118), so the request falls through to the non-attachment API branch — silently sending a plain request to an attachment URL instead of attaching, or attaching nothing without any user-visible error.
findings.impact: New regression introduced by the secondary fix: when the LLM emits a malformed/empty file param during an attach request, the tool now silently no-ops (or produces a spurious API call) instead of raising or attaching. Previously the fallback to all_files at least caused an attempt to attach whatever files were present. This defeats AC3 in the malformed-param corner case for both Jira and Confluence attach flows.
findings.recommendation: Filter falsy names before the guard: `requested_file_names = [n for n in requested_file_names if n]`. That keeps `{"file": ""}` / `{"file": null}` in the 'no names requested' bucket and preserves the intended contract (drop fallback only when the LLM actually named something that didn't match).

findings.problem: The messages_with_files comprehension has no role filter, so any GeneratedMessage with non-empty file_names — regardless of role — can win the max(history_index) selection. The ticket description and the docstring both say 'most recent USER turn'. Today all internal message-construction sites only set file_names on user-role messages, but UpsertHistoryRequest is a REST endpoint that accepts arbitrary-role GeneratedMessage payloads from callers; a non-user message at the highest history_index would then shadow the real last user upload.
findings.impact: Under a REST-driven history import that includes an assistant-role message with file_names at the top history_index, the scoping picks that assistant turn's files and silently omits the real most-recent user turn — the opposite of AC1.
findings.recommendation: Add a role check to the comprehension: `if m.role == ChatRole.USER and getattr(m, "file_names", None) and m.history_index is not None`. Import ChatRole (or reuse the existing string sentinel used elsewhere in the module). This makes the code match the docstring's stated contract and closes the REST-import attack surface.

findings.problem: If the user edits their most-recent turn to REMOVE all files (a plausible correction flow), `_get_unique_messages_from_history` last-write-wins keeps the edited-empty version; that message drops out of `messages_with_files`; `max(history_index)` then walks BACK to a prior turn that still has files, and those files are collected — the exact cross-turn leak the fix was meant to prevent, in a narrow edge case. The single-turn edit-to-empty case IS covered by test_edited_message_last_write_wins_within_latest_turn, but the multi-turn variant (edit turn N to empty when turn N-1 had files) is not.
findings.impact: AC4 leaks in this specific flow: the assistant would attach files from a prior turn after the user explicitly removed all files from the most recent turn. Low real-world probability but semantically the same class of bug as the ticket.
findings.recommendation: Product decision needed: (a) accept the edge case — document it as out-of-scope for this ticket and add a regression test asserting the current behavior so it's explicit; OR (b) tighten the semantics so 'user removed files from the latest turn' means 'no files this request' (i.e. compute latest_turn_index over ALL user messages within scope, not just those with files). Option (b) is a ~5-line change plus a test.
